Mkhondo: The silent war

By: Anina Peens | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What happened at Pampoenkraal?

Unique Selling Point:
We visit Mkhodo to investigate the events leading up to the tragic incident at the farm Pampoenkraal in Mkhondo during which two brothers were killed.

Summary:
Small farmers, land beneficiaries, commercial farmers, farmworkers, traditional leaders and the community of Mkhondo are losing the battle against crime in the area. Livestock herders who are tasked with counting stock daily, don’t report the missing numbers to the farmers anymore because they know, they would have to find the missing animals. If they track them, they always track them back to the same area where a syndicate is believed to operate. Criminals here attack the herders for tracking the farmers’ livestock, accusing the herders of siding with the white community. Farmworkers who don’t want to become part of the syndicates are intimidated to the extend where they are too afraid to attend events and social gatherings in the evenings or over weekends, because that is where the criminal await them. That is where they are attacked and killed. Over the last five years, crime has intensified and the community say, it is now completely out of control. And after what happened at Pampoen in April, they see no end in sight. On the contrary, they say, the war has only just begun.


Further information:
A sheep is strapped to a pole, upside down, left to die. Twenty-four lambs fall to their death as they are thrown off a cliff. The message is clear: “We are in charge and there is nothing you can do about it”.
A small-scale farmer is stabbed in the neck, chest and back and left to die. After he miraculously recovers in hospital, he opens a case of attempted murder against one of the most notorious criminals in the Piet Retief area. The case disappears.
A month later, the same criminal is caught red handed stealing sheep. He is filmed while spilling the beans. He admits that he has stolen more than a 100 sheep the previous week. He says he stole them from Piet Rabe’s farm. Since June last year, Piet Rabe had lost 350 sheep to livestock theft, he sold off the rest of his herd and gave up the fight. He says, they finally broke him.

Commercial farmer Bheki Mabuse (David Mabuse’s first cousin) stands defeated between his ready-to-harvest maize crops. They have been destroyed. His brand-new fences were cut, and stolen cattle from surrounding farms stampeded though the crops, taking Mabuse’s cattle along with them. The cattle are chased with such high intensity speed that some of them die of exhaustion along the way.

Small farmers, land beneficiaries, commercial farmers, farmworkers, traditional leaders and the community of Mkhondo are losing the battle against criminals in the area. Livestock herders who are tasked with counting stock daily, don’t report the missing numbers to the farmers anymore because they know, they would have to find the missing animals. If they track them, they always track them back to the same area where a syndicate is believed to operate. Criminals here attack the herders for tracking the farmers’ livestock, accusing the herders of siding with the white community. Farmworkers who don’t want to become part of the syndicate are intimidated to the extend where they are too afraid to attend events and social gatherings because that is where the criminal await them. That is where they are attacked and killed.

When did this start?
Livestock theft has always been a problem in the area, because the farmland here borders with Swaziland. As is the case with farmland in the Free state bordering with Lesotho, there is no fence and no control between farmland on the Mpumalanga highveld and Swaziland. And although the community say that the police are assisting them in fighting crime, criminals are hardly ever prosecuted.

Over the last five years, crime has intensified and the community say, it is now completely out of control. And after what happened at Pampoen in April, they see no end in sight. On the contrary, they say, the war has only just begun.

But what happened over the last five years? Why are the farm workers and farming community so angry with the farmers?
“It is not the farm workers. The criminals come from outside” the farmworkers say.

In 2015, Shishiliza Farmers Association was established. An NPO registered in Newcastle. The registered address; a stand number in Barry Hertzog park in Newcastle belonging to Solomon Mthabela, chairman of Shishiliza. Farmworkers between Piet Retief, Dirkiesdorp, Driefontein, Wakkerstroom and Ermelo were mobilized to become members. Shishiliza announced that it was funded by the department of Rural Development and Land Reform to distribute land to farmworkers. But first, they had to take the land from the commercial farmers. These targeted commercial farmers are not exclusively white farmers, they include the black farmers who either bought their own land, or they are land beneficiaries of the state.
Those opposing Shishiliza were victimised, intimidated and threatened, especially the black farmers. These farmers and farm workers were dubbed ‘Sicathalala’ meaning “Dogs attached to chains” referring to black people, siding with whites.

In order to become a member of Shishiliza, a person has to donate one cow. They are promised an offspring every six month (a cow’s gestation period is 9 months). In exchange for the cow, Shishiliza mediates on behalf of the farmworkers, between government and the farmers promising the community farmland. In addition to the cow, members also have to pay a monthly membership fee of R250.

The deregistration of Shishiliza commenced in 2017 due to tax-noncompliance and the NPO was finally deregistered in August 2020. No valid email address or cellphone number could be found. The registered address is vacant land. The NPO has no connection to the department of Rural Development and Land Reform and has no mandate from the state to redistribute land. Mthabela is also director of five other companies that have been deregistered due to non-compliance.

Bongokosi Dube, a local farmworker and livestock trader is chairman of Shishiliza at Pampoen. Pampoenkraal is the farm where the incident happened, but Pampoen is referred to as the area between Dirkiesdorp, Driefontein, Piet Retief, Daggakraal, Wakkerstroom, Donkerhoek and Geelhoutboom.
There are about a thousand people living in the Pampoen area. About 150 people live on the Pampoenkraal farm of whom only ten were former employees of the actual farming operations. The rest were never employed by Pampoenkraal and never asked for work. They hail mainly from Kwazulu Natal. It is believed that the majority of residents on Pampoen, are members of Shishaliza.
On the day of the incident, Dube led the protest.

Why was there a protest at Pampoenkraal farm on 9 April?

The Greyling family have been farming in the area for many years. Pampoenkraal is one of their farms. Livestock theft has been rife on the farm over the last fifteen years. One of the family’s patriarchs who is 90 years old now, lives on the farm. Up until the death of his son in 2008, the pair farmed together. In 2010, Greyling appointed Werner Potgieter as farm manager.
Potgieter’s first priority was to eradicate livestock theft.

He formed ties with a group called ‘Oneyatstsotsi’, established in 2017 by Vusi Zondo (small-scale farmer) and the farmworkers’ community, to fight livestock theft and crime. They started tracking the livestock thieves and arresting them, handing them over to the police.
Potgieter meanwhile pulled in the reins for farmworkers at Pampoenkraal. He instated a clocking system for workers to monitor working hours. Many of the workers grew dissatisfied with Potgieter's management style. Most of them joined Shishiliza.

The first protest demanding Potgieter’s resignation was at the gate of his farm Bovenvallei (3km from Pampoenkraal) in June 2020, in the middle of the lockdown. The next protest came in August of 2020 during which a memorandum was handed to Potgieter’s stepson Cornelius Greyling, one of the accused on the Coke case. The protesters did not want to hand over the memorandum to Potgieter as they said, ‘he is not a Greyling and he does not belong on Pampoenkraal’.
The memorandum demanded grazing land, irrigated land and electricity. They also accused Potgieter of killing 14 cattle, belonging to an alleged stock thief and demanded Potgieter pay back the cattle. Potgieter denied that he killed the cattle and indicated to them that he has already signed the approval for electricity on Pampoenkraal and that they had to wait for Eskom to install the electricity. He declined to give them land.

Since then, farmworkers working for Potgieter received calls and text messages, threatening and intimidating them. Farmworkers say they are threatened that their houses will be burnt if they go to work at Pampoenkraal. The protesters called the farmworkers who still wanted to work ‘Sicathalalas’ and blocked the three-way stop next to Pampoenkraal regularly.
Farm workers from across the entire area say, when the road is blocked, they have to pay the protesters R50 to pass. If not, they threaten to kill them.

On the day of the incident on 9 April, it is believed the protest was led by Shishiliza members and a ‘hitman’ was hired to kill Potgieter and Zondo. This hitman is not a local, he hailed from Johannesburg. His name was Amos Coka and he was one of the brothers who was shot and killed.

The farming community say that the killing of the two Coka brothers will be avenged, and they expect that the war is only now gaining momentum;
“It is no longer only about livestock theft; they will avenge the death of the brothers”.

Press Release:


The Silent War

On the Mpumalanga Highveld, a silent war erupts every night as the community fights livestock theft and crime that has been spiralling out of control over the last few years. In April, a group of farmworkers protested – ostensibly for employment – at the entrance of the farm Pampoenkraal near Piet Retief. Two brothers, Mgcini and Zenzele Coka, joined the protest. When a scuffle between the protesters and a group of farmers broke out, the Coka brothers were killed and led to the arrest of four farmers and a farm worker who were released on bail three weeks later. At the end of May, another farmer and his entire farm management team were arrested on charges of murder. Court proceedings have been marked by crowds gathering outside. Carte Blanche investigates the underlying issues that led to the clash and asks: what lies behind the tensions that finally spilled over?

Producer: Anina Peens | Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli

Script:


Mkhondo: The Silent War

Opening
On 9 April, it was reported that a group of farm workers of which brothers, Mgcini and Zenzele Coka were part, protested at the entrance of the farm Pampoenkraal near Piet Retief in Mpumalanga. They were allegedly protesting for jobs. A scuffle between protesters and a group of farmers broke out and the Coka brothers were killed. Four farmers and one farm workers were arrested and released on bail three weeks later. Large crowds gathered outside the Piet Retief Magistrate court. They were told that Pampoenkraal farm will burn.

CREDIT: FACEBOOK: MKHONDO RADI0 STATION
SUBTITLE
3’23”-3’26”
“This farm will and must burn down”
LINK
Tensions were very high at this court, and this followed the killing of the Coka brothers. And now two more farmers have been added to the charge sheet. Yet the issues that led to the tensions of this Piet Retief farming community remain unresolved.
VO
These tensions revolve around land issues while escalating livestock theft is aggravating the situation. Commercial farmer Bheki Mabuse says, it’s a daily war against criminality in the area.
SUPER@ BHEKI MABUSE: COMMECIAL FARMER
00:02:33-00:02:49
I think the stealing has been happening for about three to four years. But from last year to this year, it’s worse.”
VO
Farmers say, criminals infiltrated the area. Owner of Pampoenkraal farm, Werner Potgieter says this causes a divide in the otherwise close-knit farming community.
SUPER@ WERNER POTGIETER: FARMER: PAMPOENKRAAL
“My verhouding met my gemeenskap was baie goed, tot op ‘n sekere stadium”
MAC
“En watse stadium was daai?”
SUPER
“Die stadium wat mens begin optree het teen sekere elemente en teen misdaad begin optree het”
VO
The farm Pampoenkraal is situated in an area called, Pampoen.
LINK
“This area is referred to as Pampoen and is nestled in the valleys between Dirkiesdorp, Wakkerstroom and Driefontein about an hour’s drive from Piet Retief. It is estimated that about a thousand people call this area home”
VO
Land issues in the area, are centered around Potgieter. He took ownership of Pampoenkraal farm in 2008. He says he has always allowed his worker’s cattle to graze his farm, but that outsiders came in and started to share in the benefit. About 150 people live on the farm of which only a few are farm workers.
CLIP 00153
13’ 31’03’
SUPER@WERNER POTGIETER: FARMER: PAMPOENKRAAL
“Hulle bring beeste van buite af in, hulle ploeg grond in lande waar daar nie mag geploeg word nie, hulle jaag hulle beeste in kampe in waar daar nie ‘n ooreenkoms is nie wat hulle reg gee om hulle beeste in te jaag nie. En dit is wat die spanning veroorsaak.”
TRANSLATION
“They bring cattle from outside onto my land. They plough land that they are not permitted to plough, and their cattle are grazing in camps, and we don’t have an agreement allowing that. That is what is causing the tension”

VO
A mediating body representing farmworkers was formed to address the land issue.
The farmworkers and labor tenant’s association was established by BH Hlatshwayo about five years ago. Hlatshwayo represents farmworkers from Mpumalanga, KZN and Free State. But the majority of his members are based around Mkhondo.

DOUBLE STRAP
SUPER@ BH HLATSWAYO: FARM RESIDENTS, WORKERS AND LABOUR TENANTS ASSOCIATION WRITE OUT FULL STRAPDONT STOP ON ASS.
“We are the voice of the people that are living on the farm. Because most of the time you find that the residents and the farm workers do not know their rights, what is their right…because sometimes you find that the farmers are violating their rights.”

VO
Potgieter says Hlatswayo gives people rights to land.

SUPER@WERNER POTGIETER: FARMER: PAMPOENKRAAL
CLIP 00153
12’53’03’
“Die probleem is die verwagting word geskep deur Bongani en sy organisasie. En daar word sekere regte deur hom aan hierdie mense voorgegee dat dit hulle reg is, en dit is nie hulle reg nie. En dit is wat die spanning veroorsaak”
TRANSLATION
“The problem is that Bongani and his organization create expectation amongst the people. He gives certain rights to the people that are not their rights. This is what causes the tension”

VO
Hlatswayo says based on the labor tenant Act of 1996, those who are associated to farm workers or labor tenants have a right to the land.

DOUBLE STRAP
SUPER@ BH HLATSWAYO: LEADER: FARM RESIDENT WORKERS AND LABOUR TENANTS ASS.
CLIP 00153
23’54’22’
“This issue of land, people have been claiming the land and even the department, they have been applying Section 16 of the labor tenant Act and that process is another process. But for temporary they were asking, those farm residents for grazing cattle and ploughing for the people”

VO
Hlatswayo led a group of residents to Potgieter’s farm to hand over a memorandum of demands.

SUPER@ BH HLATSWAYO: LEADER: FARM RESIDENT WORKERS AND LABOUR TENANTS ASS.
CLIP 00153
22’09’00’
“I am the person that was signing and handing over. We were making the request to solve this fighting, to give this resident at the farm Pampoenkraal the land to grazing for cattle, all of the cattle must be in this camp”

VO
The memorandum demanded the resignation of Potgieter and key members of his management team. Hlatswayo also accused Potgieter of poisoning the farm residents’ cattle and demanded replacement. They further demanded electricity for residents as well as ploughable land. Potgieter denied he poisoned the cattle and dismissed the request for his resignation. He did approve electricity to be installed by the municipality but declined the request for land.

SUPER@WERNER POTGIETER: FARMER: PAMPOENKRAAL
00’09’10’15’
“Hoe kan ek meer grond vir hulle gee? Die grond wat huidiglik is boer ons self op. So dit is produktiewe grond wat hulle net wil he. Ek kannie net goed vir hulle gee nie.”
TRANSLATION
“How can I give them the land that we are farming on? It is productive farmland that they want. I can’t just give it to them.”

VO
When their demand for land was denied, protests started and the road next to Pampoenkraal was frequently blocked. Farm workers say they were stopped by people among protestors - with unknown affiliations -- who demanded money from the passersby.

LINK
CLIP 00225
“This intersection next to Pampoenkraal connects the towns of Dirkiesdorp, Amersfoort and various other towns. It is a busy road used by farmers, farm workers, school buses and trucks.

VO
The informal roadblock prevented farm workers from passing.

SUPER@FARM WORKER ANONYMOUS
00153
29’42’00
“If you are driving past there, they are always asking for money, it doesn’t matter how many times you are gonna drive past there, they still want you to pay every time you drive past there. And then I say to them, you guys are blocking me, and you are protesting against this farm at Pampoen, but I don’t work at Pampoen. Then they say, ja, it doesn’t matter you are working for a white guy”

VO
To be represented by Hlatswayo’s organization also comes at a price.

SUPER@ BH HLATSWAYO: LEADER: FARM RESIDENT WORKERS AND LABOUR
CLIP 0153
15’26’11
“To be a member of the organization you need to pay the application for membership of R250 for annual and then to making the organization to getting to move you are paying the subscription of 150 per month”

VO
The organization has 700 members. Each members pays a subscription fee from February to November. In total, the organization collects more than a million Rand annually from farm workers.

VO

Meanwhile, farmworkers and herders say they are living in fear as the violence with which the livestock thieves operate intensified over the last year. Mabuse and other farmers say, their herders are too afraid to report missing stock, as they know they would have to trace them back to the same criminals.

SUPER@ BHEKI MABUSE: COMMERCIAL FARMER
00:04:25-00:046
There is a place called Hugu that side and they are scared of it. I went there myself put them in my van. I took my big gun and went straight there. I beaten the boys who stole from me. I told them that from that day I want to locate my cows and I found them with the ropes on their heads. So it has been upsetting to us.

VO
Herders and guards are cornered by the criminals in the evenings and over weekends, at social events and gatherings.

SUPER@ BHEKI MABUSE: COMMERCIAL FARMER
00:03:31-00:04:11
the shepherds are scared because when they find them they are stabbed, beaten. I have a child who was stabbed. My neighbor also had someone who was stabbed.

VO

Farmers, workers and herders know who all the criminals are.

UPSOUND HORSE CHASE BLUR FACES OF MEN ON HORSE
00:00:27-00:00:35
Farmer: Why did you run yesterday?
00:00: 35-00:00:56
Boy: what do you want from me, I didn`t do anything,
00:01:03-00:01:12
Boy: why did you chase me, I don`t anything about the Cattle, what did I do?

VO
Mabuse says the criminals are all young men, under the age of 25 and no one is spared their revolt.

SUPER@ BHEKI MABUSE: COMMERCIAL FARMER
00:04:37-00:04:56
No, they don’t choose, whether black or what or you are a granny. They take the cattle from their kraals at night. You would find that the granny lost her husband and they can take about four or five cows and take with them.

VO
The ruthlessness with which the criminals operate is of great concern.

SUPER@ BHEKI MABUSE: COMMERCIAL FARMER
00:01:42-00:02:13
“What was also painful to me was that the lambs were chopped and dumped on the way. They took the ewe/the mothers instead. They dumped the lambs.
00:02:14-00:02:15
Makfolen: They just dump them and not use them?
00:02:15-00:02:31
Mabuza: They don’t use them. Its painful just losing one sheep so how about when they cut the lambs and take ewe/the mother. It’s very painful.

VO
On one farm, 18 lambs were ripped from their mothers and thrown to their death down a cliff. Vusi Zondo says, these acts are messages of anarchy indicating that the criminals are untouchable. Zondo established an anti-stocktheft movement called Wanjwa Tsotsi

SUPER@ VUSI ZONDO: LEADER: WANJWA TSOTSI
00:03:09-00:03:48
“I saw that black and white farmer’s livestock was stolen and I decided to do something different…I looked at its strategy of beating up the thieves. I noticed that we might get ourselves arrested.”

VO
Wanya Tsotsi comprises of footprint tracers, herders and informants, tracking down criminals and handing them to the police.
Zondo says, there has always been peace in the community, and that the tension is brought in from outside.

SUPER@ VUSI ZONDO: LEADER: WANJWA TSOTSI
“You see my son, if you don’t live around here and now you want to be involved to matter of this area and you want create problems. The outsiders want to push for their own agenda”

VO
Potgieter joined forces with Wanjwa Tsotsi to curb livestock theft in the area.

SUPER@ WERNER POTGIETER: FARMER: PAMPOENKRAAL
CLIP 00088
14’30’53’09’
“Mense is betrokke by misdaad, as hulle betrokke is by misdaad word dit opgevolg en dan word daar arrestasies gemaak en die mense hou nie daarvan om arresteer te word nie. Die misdaad is ‘n baie groot bedryf in die omgewing daar is baie geld daarby betrokke”

VO
Hlatswayo says, the farmers must leave the crime fighting to the police.

SUPER@ BH HLATSWAYO: LEADER: FARM RESIDENT WORKERS AND LABOUR
“Most of the time the white farmers are accusing the resident, the people that stay on the farm, they are stealing their livestock. That is true, but they are not following the right procedures to investigate”

VO
According to the Mpumalanga provincial police, 121 cases of stock theft were opened since January 2021 at Piet Retief and Dirkiesdorp stations.

VO
Potgieter and Andries Pienaar were arrested for murder and kidnapping on 17 May, linked to the 9April incident at Pampoenkraal. Hlatswayo says, he brought the charges

SUPER@ BH HLATSWAYO: LEADER: FARM RESIDENT WORKERS AND LABOUR
“Yes, it is our organization that bring the charges to the court, because we are not happy the way that mister Potgieter and his crew, what they are doing at the farm.

VO
Potgieter and Pienaar were released on bail but on 28 May Potgieter was arrested again along with his management team. They are accused of allegedly killing stock thieves in August 2020. These charges were also brought by Hlatswayo.

They were told that Pampoenkraal farm will burn. UPSOUND CREDIT: FACEBOOK: MKHONDO RADI0 STATION SUBTITLE 3’23”-3’26” “This farm will and must burn down” LINK Tensions were very high at this court, and this followed the killing of the Coka brothers. VO These tensions revolve around land issues while escalating livestock theft is aggravating the situation. Commercial farmer Bheki Mabuse says, it’s a daily war against criminality in the area. SUPER@ BHEKI MABUSE: COMMECIAL FARMER 00:02:33-00:02:49 I think the stealing has been happening for about three to four years. CLIP 00153 23’54’22’ “This issue of land, people have been claiming the land and even the department, they have been applying Section 16 of the labor tenant Act and that process is another process. These charges were also brought by Hlatswayo.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: We visit Mkhodo to investigate the events leading up to the tragic incident at the farm Pampoenkraal in Mkhondo during which two brothers were killed.

If they track them, they always track them back to the same area where a syndicate is believed to operate.
